headline: Home Minister: Salman Muqtadir’s BNP extortion claim is sweeping, no case filed
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed questioned content creator Salman Muqtadir's Facebook Live allegations following an attack on his studio, stating that a sweeping claim about the BNP was made without filing a case.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has called content creator Salman Muqtadir's remarks after his studio was attacked and vandalized "controversial." The minister questioned why Salman had not filed a case regarding the incident, which occurred Saturday night at his "BrownFish" studio in Dhaka's ECB Chattar area.

Salman had posted a Facebook Live video showing the damage to his studio and surrounding facilities. He initially suggested the attack might have been personal but later indicated it was related to the housing project where his studio is located. He also remarked, "Please don't worry. This is normal in Bangladesh."

The Home Minister addressed Salman's allegations regarding extortion and the BNP. Salahuddin noted that Salman admitted no money was demanded but stated he would have paid if asked. The minister dismissed Salman's claim that the BNP is a "party of extortionists" as a "sweeping allegation."

Police suspect a land dispute involving a 35-katha plot may be behind the attack. Preliminary investigations suggest a group, acting on behalf of a retired senior military officer, attempted to forcibly take possession of the property under the cover of darkness. The attack targeted the company office and other structures at New Gini Properties, not just Salman's studio.

Spent bullet casings and locally made weapons were recovered from the scene. The incident took place in Manikdi Namapara under Cantonment Police Station. Legal proceedings are underway, and further details are expected as the investigation progresses.

headline: Over 2,000 candidates recommended for primary teacher posts face delays
summary: Recommended candidates are staging a sit-in at Shahbag, demanding appointment letters after being excluded from the process in 61 districts.
details: Over 200 recommended candidates for government primary school assistant teacher positions staged a sit-in protest at Shahbag in Dhaka on Sunday.
The protesters, who gathered in front of the National Museum, are demanding the immediate issuance of appointment letters for those who were finally recommended for the job.
According to the candidates, more than 2,000 recommended candidates across 61 districts have been excluded from the recruitment process during the verification stage.
A delegation of the protesters visited the Secretariat to meet with ministry officials to discuss the issue, though details of the meeting were not immediately available.
While protests continue in the capital, the Rajshahi district has issued appointment letters to 22 candidates in a second phase of recruitment.
The appointment letters in Rajshahi were issued based on the results of the Assistant Teacher Recruitment Examination-2025 under the Directorate of Primary Education.
caption:
Over 2,000 recommended candidates for primary teacher posts have been excluded from recruitment across 61 districts.

Over 200 recommended candidates for government primary school assistant teacher positions staged a sit-in protest at Shahbag in Dhaka on Sunday.

The protesters, who gathered in front of the National Museum, are demanding the immediate issuance of appointment letters for those who were finally recommended for the job.

According to the candidates, more than 2,000 recommended candidates across 61 districts have been excluded from the recruitment process during the verification stage.

A delegation of the protesters visited the Secretariat to meet with ministry officials to discuss the issue, though details of the meeting were not immediately available.

While protests continue in the capital, the Rajshahi district has issued appointment letters to 22 candidates in a second phase of recruitment.

The appointment letters in Rajshahi were issued based on the results of the Assistant Teacher Recruitment Examination-2025 under the Directorate of Primary Education.
